html:
The Wateree were a Siouan people of the Piedmont of South Carolina, living along the Wateree River near today's Camden.

The Spanish expedition of Juan Pardo met them in 1566 and called their chiefdom Guatari. They lived close to the Congaree, Cheraw and Sugaree. English traders from Charles Town later bought deerskins and slaves from them. After the Yamasee War of 1715 their numbers fell sharply, and the survivors joined the Catawba. The Wateree River keeps their name.
sum: The Wateree were a Siouan people of the Piedmont of South Carolina, living along the Wateree River near today's Camden.
